hypotheses.reasoning: Logins were healthy until 22:44 (for example #74, 175ms). At 22:44:19 the third-party identity provider (idp.example/oauth2/token) became slow: 4.2s (#77), then 7.7s (#80). From 22:45:13 its calls hung until the 30s timeout (#84, #97). account-svc's calls to auth-svc for tokens then timed out the same way (#85, #98). Those hanging calls filled account-svc's 50-connection HTTP pool to auth-svc (#101) and caused pool checkout timeouts (#108). account-svc then returned 503s, which edge-proxy passed on as POST /login 5xx (#96, #106, #114, #117). Those lines are downstream symptoms. I found no deploy lines, and the DB, cache and audit consumer look normal.
The identity provider is a third party and may have been degraded. But its calls hung until they timed out rather than failing fast, and there was no 5xx or status-page signal from it.

verdict.recommendedAction: Contact the identity provider (idp.example) or check its status. In auth-svc, lower the IdP call timeout from 30s to a few seconds and add a circuit breaker with fast fail or fallback. Cap the time account-svc waits on auth-svc so hung calls can't fill its 50-connection pool.
